title: Our God, How Firm His Promise Stands
description: Our God, How Firm His Promise Stands in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 40, headed “Our comfort in the covenant made with Christ”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our God, how firm his pro-mise stands, E'en when he hides his face! He trusts in our Re-deem-er's hands His glo-ry and his grace.

lines: Our God, how firm his promise stands,
E'en when he hides his face!
He trusts in our Redeemer's hands
Then why, my soul, these sad complaints,
Since Christ and we are one;
Thy God is faithful to his saints,
Beneath his smiles my heart has liv'd,
I praise his Name for grace receiv'd,
And trust him for the rest.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
